body:
Released in [`@emseepea/testing` 0.22.0](https://github.com/emseepea/emseepea/releases/tag/%40emseepea%2Ftesting%400.22.0). Following Tom Howard’s explicit decision to remove the limit, native Claude and Codex conversations no longer reject more than three advertised MCP calls. There is no replacement count ceiling or maxToolCalls option. The CLI evidence validator also accepts longer journeys, checks count consistency, and does not assume one provider turn per call. Claude’s native four-turn flag is also removed: the first candidate retained it and added a four-turn parser ceiling, which rejected all three live four-read trials. Both count ceilings are now absent. The failed candidate remains recorded in [Release run 37922640488](https://github.com/emseepea/emseepea/actions/runs/37922640488); the repaired candidate was qualified separately. Tool-free judges retain their original limits.

Advertised-tool restrictions, per-send timeouts, cancellation, and output checks, isolation, and application assertions remain enforced. Parser checks retain all forty calls and their results and hashed evidence. The real native timetable qualification requires four authoritative MCP reads and correct route-to-time associations in every trial. Existing independent meaning judgments remain required; the failed candidate was not retried.

Exact-source qualification, Source Quality, Release, and Publish passed. Testing 0.22.0 and all eleven initializer updates are verified on npm latest; the testing guide is deployed. ADR-0116 records the approved replacement for the original configurable-budget proposal. This release removes the count-exhaustion failure; it does not claim new transcripts for unrelated provider failures.
